They were regenerated per the ADR-019 recipe from a C-only release build (clang-cl, -Duse_sdl3=enabled, -Duse_rust=disabled) of tag c-reference/final in a separate worktree, state-hash and --sndhash chains; the .snd PCM chains were unchanged by the regeneration. DEVIATION from Misc/harness/README.md's 'regenerate only from a c-reference/* tag': no such tag exists -- the repository has zero tags, and ROADMAP.md defers c-reference/phase0 through phase3 on the PLAN section 3 MinGW/GNU-Makefile decision. The darwin-arm64 set has the same provenance shape (generated from plain commit dfe80297, not a tag). These were generated from a release, use_rust=disabled build at the recorded commit, which is what 'the C reference build' means while C remains the oracle. Resolved 2026-09-19: the tag c-reference/final now exists (fb372b7d) and is the only generator.

Compiler independence was measured, not assumed. CI builds Windows with clang-cl (build-windows.yml), while these were generated with MSVC cl. A separate clang-cl 22.1.8 C-only release build reproduces the 8 regenerated entries byte-identically (re-measured 2026-09-04 against the current set) on both the demo state-hash chain and the --sndhash mixer PCM chain, so the CI --check leg is valid against this set. The ADR-010 same-platform rule still stands: do not compare these against a non-Windows build.

Four build/toolchain combinations are verified against the 8 regenerated entries, all identical on both chains: C-only/cl (the generator), mixed/cl, C-only/clang-cl, mixed/clang-cl. The mixed builds carry the full Phase 7 Rust port, so --check pins the port against the C engine's per-frame state hashes rather than only against itself.

Coverage is the 11 entries this machine has data for: the 8 shareware-tier entries plus registered-tier e3m6-trains, save-e2m1 and music-wav. The five remaining registered/rerelease entries and the four mod-tier entries have no local data and no goldens here; run_corpus.py --check skips them without failing, so a green --check on this platform has not exercised them.

corpus.json pins a sha256 on each entry's required data, and entry_available hard-skips on mismatch, so these goldens are tied to exactly the 1.06 pak0 that CI's fetch_shareware.py produces (identical in shareware and registered installs).
Goldens are derived per-frame FNV-1a state hashes, not game data.
Generated from release builds only; debug builds run the stability gate but are not compared against these (FP results may differ by optimization level, ADR-010).
The headless RNG stream intentionally differs from a windowed run, so these only ever compare headless runs against headless runs.
Never hand-edit. Regenerate with run_corpus.py --generate (and again with --sndhash) from a C-only release build on windows-x86_64.
